## 固定收益市場主線

10月5日長天期美國公債走跌，服務業需求強勁、企業成本上升的新證據，使借款利率持續承壓。10年期美債殖利率上升3.4個基點至5.307%，30年期上升4.3個基點至5.664%，2年期則下降1.4個基點至4.813%。9月服務業調查顯示，整體經濟招募放緩，並未使需求降溫或產能限制消退。ISM價格指數升至2022年7月以來最高，S&P Global則錄得2021年7月以來最強勁的服務業擴張。

賣壓集中在短期政策展望以外的較長天期。10年期實質殖利率上升3.5個基點，長期通膨補償小降0.1個基點、略為抵銷漲幅，名目殖利率因而上升3.4個基點。油價下跌約2%、股市上漲，美國企業債利差也小幅收窄，卻未能阻止長期借款利率走高。這個交易日既呈現經濟活動的韌性，也顯示市場提供長期資金時，仍要求更高的報酬。

歐洲財政壓力在銀行與匯市的影響更為明顯。法國銀行的違約保障成本超過歐洲主要同業，歐元跌至17個月低點，西班牙宣布提前大選。ECB官員持續強調抑制通膨，同時區分新一波能源壓力與薪資、價格設定行為的持久變化。巴西則形成鮮明對比：Flávio Bolsonaro意外在首輪大選領先，投資人重新評估財政整頓前景，帶動利率交換利率大跌。

資金昂貴並未使借款停頓，但條件與急迫程度愈來愈能區分不同發行人。一筆$50億的AI基礎設施貸款以約11%的殖利率向投資人推介，設備證券化也開始納入相當比例的GPU資產。美國地方政府借款人寧可延後再融資，也不願放棄原先追求的利息節省；Virgin Media O2的寬頻整併遇到阻礙，威脅降低槓桿的計畫，債券因而重挫。

## 服務業需求持續推升長天期美債殖利率

9月ISM服務業指數由55.4降至54.9，活動僅溫和放緩，仍連續二十七個月擴張。數值低於路透調查的55.2共識，也低於Trading Economics另列的55預期。十三個產業回報成長，四個產業萎縮，包括礦業與營建業。占經濟較大比重的服務業仍有廣泛的企業擴張，並非只靠科技投資熱潮支撐。

商業活動指數從61.7降至56.5，低於61.5預期；新訂單由60.9降至59.8，也低於60.3預測。不過，就業由47.8回升至50.1，優於48預期，結束連續兩個月的萎縮。服務業產出成長放緩，企業整體卻回報招聘改善，與週五非農就業報告招募疲弱的訊號不同。

成本與交貨壓力更加明顯。支付價格指數從72.6升至74.0，高於72.9預測，也是近七個月第六次超過70。受訪企業提到銅、柴油、鋼鐵、石油相關產品與記憶體產品漲價。供應商交貨指數由51.3升至53.2，交貨放慢已持續二十二個月；未完成訂單連續八個月增加，指數達56.6，為2022年7月以來最高。

ISM服務業商業調查委員會主席Steve Miller表示，企業最常提及的供應鏈問題是關稅與燃料成本，其中燃料成本被提到的頻率，約為其他任何單一問題的兩倍。另一方面，出口訂單八個月來首次跌破50。內需仍支撐活動，外部訂單卻轉弱，服務客戶所需成本也上升。部分企業另提到組織重整，以及運用AI工具提高效率。

S&P Global的服務業終值呈現更強的加速：指數由8月的56.5升至58.8，略高於58.7初值與共識，連續六個月擴張，力道為2021年7月以來最強。科技業領先，消費相關企業、工業與醫療保健業也加速。綜合指數終值由56.0升至58.4，符合預期。

這份調查的新訂單增速創逾四年最快，由強勁內需帶動。就業連續三個月增加，招聘速度為2022年6月以來最快；訂單超過產能，未完成訂單連續十九個月累積。天然氣與勞動成本推升投入成本，漲幅達2022年11月以來最高，企業售價通膨則是略逾一年來第二高。企業信心升至一年高點。

兩份調查對整體活動增速的變化看法不同，細項卻都未指向服務業需求普遍轉弱。訂單持續增加、招聘恢復或加速、未完成訂單累積，加上明顯成本壓力，是兩者共有的訊號。對聯準會而言，整體經濟新增雇員減少，與需求已冷卻到足以減輕價格設定壓力，是不同的情況。週一數據較支持前者，而非後者。

BMO Capital Markets策略師Vail Hartman認為，ISM報告符合通膨壓力增加與名目成長強勁的情況，強化近期債市賣壓背後的力量。彭博盤中美債報導記錄，指標10年期與30年期殖利率至少上升7個基點，分別達5.34%與5.70%，為2002年以來最高。10月5日的每日殖利率則為10年期5.307%、30年期5.664%。

短端殖利率下降、長端殖利率上升，使每日殖利率曲線變陡。5年期小升0.4個基點至5.058%，2年與10年期利差擴大4.8個基點至49.4個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大5.7個基點至85.1個基點。相較一週前，2年期下降11.9個基點，10年期與30年期分別上升7.0與11.6個基點，2年與10年期利差擴大18.9個基點。短期政策展望帶來的利率壓力緩解，並未延伸至長期融資。

10年期實質殖利率上升3.5個基點至2.944%，損益兩平通膨率小降0.1個基點至2.363%。與一個月前相比，也主要是實質利率上升：名目殖利率增加52.4個基點，實質殖利率增加51.4個基點，損益兩平通膨率增加1.0個基點。調查反映的新一波通膨壓力，有助於解釋為何ISM整體活動放緩未能安撫債市，但當日長期通膨補償大致持平、略為下降；名目殖利率升幅主要來自實質借款成本提高。

油價稍微緩解壓力。固定收益市場收盤時，WTI每桶下跌2.03%至$89.26，布蘭特下跌1.97%至$100.24，但布蘭特仍比一個月前高8.58%。美國總統川普準備放寬某種免稅柴油的使用限制，再度嘗試降低燃料成本。這項提案處理的是當前企業壓力來源，ISM調查則反映已傳導到受訪企業的成本。

股票表現優於債券。S&P 500上漲0.66%至7,773.95，接近歷史高點；Nasdaq 100上漲0.87%，以31,076.44創新高。Morgan Stanley Wealth Management的Lisa Shalett認為，成長加速與AI熱潮對利率敏感度有限，使股市相對平穩。Nationwide的Mark Hackett則指出，獲利成長與利潤率改善，抵銷了愈來愈沉重的融資成本。

不過，股市漲勢集中在少數成分股。彭博市場分析指出，近60%的S&P 500成分股低於200日均線，約75%低於50日均線。Goldman Sachs主經紀商資料顯示，避險基金9月大部分時間增加空頭與避險部位，而非削減多頭。主要指數雖然上漲，融資及能源成本曝險較大的企業卻仍承壓。

另一篇週一分析指出，美債選擇權波動率指數MOVE約為108，接近當時VIX的七倍，兩者比值為2024年底以來最大。當日稍後的VIX讀數為15.52。這項對比顯示，即使企業當前獲利未下滑，債市與股市仍可能對風險有不同評估。美元指數上漲0.17%至102.102，黃金期貨每盎司小漲0.15%至$4,168.40。

## 法國風險蔓延至銀行，ECB權衡能源壓力

法國主權壓力更清楚地反映在銀行信用的相對定價。週一，為法國興業銀行€1,000萬、可納入紓困減記或轉股的優先債務購買5年期保障，每年需支付€10.3萬，較德意志銀行同類保障多約€1.65萬；8月底兩者成本仍相同。BNP Paribas與Crédit Agricole的違約保障費率，也明顯高於英國、德國、瑞士與西班牙主要銀行。

主權疑慮透過銀行持有的政府債券，以及影響借款人的經濟政策，傳導至銀行融資。ING策略師Jeroen van den Broek與Timothy Rahill表示，利率走高、財政疑慮再起與不確定性，打破歐元信用市場近期的平靜；法國風險表現最弱，也稍微波及周邊市場。銀行保障成本出現新的落差，是法國公債既有惡化之外，一項具體的信用市場變化。

法國公債再次落後德國公債。彭博週一交易報導中，法德10年期利差擴大10個基點至150個基點，較長天期法國與義大利債券也弱於同天期德債。這是當日壓力再度加劇，尚未超越前一週的極端水準。德國仍吸引區域內尋求較安全政府債券的需求。

匯市調整更為顯著。亞洲短線基金賣出歐元、買進美元，並觸發更多選擇權相關賣盤，歐元一度下跌0.8%至$1.1161，為2025年5月以來最低。ING的Chris Turner認為，歐元對多種主要貨幣走弱，反映財政風險溢價提高，並有進一步跌向$1.10的風險。歐元風險逆轉接近2025年3月以來最偏空的水準，但仍未達過去市場明顯恐慌時的極端程度。

西班牙則出現新的政治事件。總理桑傑士的少數政府未能通過旨在處理住房負擔危機惡化的法案，因此宣布11月29日大選。反對黨人民黨在民調領先，可能尋求與極右派Vox組成聯合政府；兩黨已在包括安達魯西亞的四個地區共同執政。Crédit Agricole的Valentin Marinov表示，西班牙消息對歐元的影響不如法國問題，但也無助於其處境。

日本投資人部位的新估計，說明法國殖利率上升未必足以重建海外需求。彭博計算，日本投資人7月持有¥23兆、折合$1,450億的法國債券，占其海外債務持有量6.6%；相對彭博全球綜合債券指數，法國是其在歐元區最大的超配部位，但持有量較去年底已下降2.5%。

近期賣壓使法國10年期債券在匯率避險後，殖利率約高於日本同天期債券40個基點。瑞穗的Masayuki Nakajima認為，考量法國財政走向的不確定性與避險成本，這項收益增幅仍可能不足。日本國內殖利率上升，提高資金匯回的吸引力；既有法債超配幅度又大，不能單看法國名目殖利率判斷外國需求。Fivestar Asset Management的Hideo Shimomura警告，若ECB不處理情勢，法國殖利率可能達7%。

前ECB執行理事Lorenzo Bini Smaghi週一在《金融時報》評論中，再度公開主張暫停讓債券持有部位自然縮減。他認為利率應是主要政策工具，資產負債表調整居次，量化緊縮應暫停，直到情勢穩定、金融市場影響更清楚。這項建議延伸再投資政策的討論，並非ECB決策，也不是限制法國利差的承諾。

國際清算銀行總經理Pablo Hernández de Cos週一就更廣泛的干預難題提出警告：政府債務接近戰後高點，赤字持續龐大，使央行更難區分市場失靈，與投資人合理重新定價財政風險。即使回應是為了維護金融穩定或貨幣政策傳導，也可能被視為協助財政融資。

他也強調，避險基金、退休基金與資產管理機構持有政府債券，其槓桿與對市場融資的依賴，會在壓力期間放大波動。他列舉2020年美國搶現金潮與2022年英國公債危機，將英格蘭銀行限定期間的購債，視為一種可能範本；但若危機更大或更持久，這類限制的可信度可能降低。數位金融加速、社群媒體、穩定幣與AI，可能加快未來壓力發展，而央行換匯額度仍是應付急迫全球流動性需求的重要工具。

ECB目前的通膨評估，並未讓寬鬆政策獲得簡單理由。德國央行總裁Joachim Nagel週一表示，上行風險占優勢，但仍沒有明確跡象顯示衝擊已廣泛傳導至薪資與價格設定。較長期的市場及專家預期仍符合2%目標。他未支持任何特定的市場隱含升息時間表，主張保有彈性、逐次會議決策。

德國天然氣情勢使他的能源警告更具體。儲氣量約為容量的59%，是2009年開始有紀錄以來同期最低，歐盟平均則為72%。營運商警告，以目前注氣速度，幾乎不可能在11月1日前達到約70%的法定目標。政府在本季較早時主要依靠公用事業與交易商，如今已指示國營SEFE在未來幾週採購並儲存天然氣。

伊朗戰爭使近期天然氣價格高於冬季價格，削弱商業儲氣誘因。Nagel批評前一個冬季後補庫速度過慢，警告冬季可能必須以更高價格擴大採購，進一步推升通膨。煉油產能受損也使成品價格上漲，乾旱、野火與肥料短缺則帶來額外食品價格風險。這些具體供給限制構成他的判斷依據，並非宣稱普遍的薪資價格反應已經展開。

ECB首席經濟學家Philip Lane另主張，在評估第二波能源壓力時，應審慎衡量回應。他說，經濟對第一波衝擊的韌性出乎預期，但新一波成本可能更明顯影響活動與通膨。除了財政、AI與整體融資條件，衝擊的持續時間、強度與傳導也很重要。他認為，歐洲AI投資規模仍太小，不足以透過資料中心建設造成顯著薪資壓力，與美國建設潮目前的總體經濟影響有別。

週一歐元區PMI終值支持經濟仍具韌性的看法。服務業指數從51.6升至53.0，與初值一致，創十個月高點；綜合指數由52.0升至53.1，為2023年4月以來最高，也使第三季成為2022年第二季以來最強的一季。S&P Global的Chris Williamson估計，調查相當於GDP季增約0.4%。

西班牙活動最強，愛爾蘭居次；德國復甦加速，義大利與法國溫和成長。服務業出口訂單結束連續三十九個月的萎縮，製造與服務業合計訂單增速創四十一個月最快，海外需求增速則為逾四年半最強。服務業招聘放緩抵銷製造業小幅改善，就業增幅減弱，但投入成本與售價的漲速都升至四個月高點。ECB面對的經濟尚未出現廣泛需求弱化，卻再度承受價格壓力，難以靠需求降溫輕易抵銷通膨壓力。

## AI融資擴及貸款與設備證券化

JPMorgan開始向投資人推介Volta Infrastructure Holdings的$50億槓桿貸款，殖利率約11%，呈現新成立AI雲端業者的高成本融資結構。初步條件為基準利率加6.25至6.5個百分點，發行價格為面額的97%至98%；加計當前基準利率與發行折價後，總殖利率約為11%。

這筆融資同時支應晶片與資料中心租賃，而非單一設備採購。其中$37億將用於購買約36,000顆Nvidia GPU，另$13億將作為信用狀的現金擔保，支持支付予Bitdeer Technologies的租金。Bitdeer與Volta合作興建挪威資料中心園區。知情人士表示，Anthropic已簽下使用該處運算容量的六年協議。

貸款採strip結構，貸款人必須同時購買兩部分的份額，貸款本金並將隨時間全數攤還。借款人為特殊目的實體Volta Tydal Holdings。債務未經評等，這項不常見的安排通常會使槓桿貸款市場最大買方群CLO無法購買。貸款人電話會議於週一紐約時間上午11時舉行，承諾出資截止日為10月14日。

Volta由前Brookfield基礎設施主管Ricard Boada與Sofia Gumuzio於今年成立。貸款條件凸顯，新雲端業者與能借助投資級企業信用支持取得融資的公司，資金成本有所不同。過去新型雲端業者的融資成本較低，而本案除晶片貸款外，也包含資料中心相關融資。Anthropic的運算容量合約提供客戶承諾，貸款價格、攤還安排與受限的買方群，則界定交付服務所需的資金條件。

GPU曝險也正進入設備資產支持債券。Stonebriar Commercial Finance正在銷售約$8.69億的ABS，GPU貸款約占擔保資產15%。交易預計本週推介、10月14日交割，預期評等介於AAA與BBB-之間，存續時間最短的證券預期取得最高短期評等。這項Rule 144A發行面向合格機構投資人。

擔保資產並非全為AI硬體。電腦與IT基礎設施是最大類別，另有油氣設備、製造業資產、企業飛機與船舶資產。Wingspire Equipment Finance上月底透過設備貸款與租賃證券化，募集逾$4.07億，GPU約占資產池20%，向機構投資人發行的證券中包括AAA級券。新揭露的比例顯示，AI硬體融資已進入多元設備資產池，而不再侷限於專門的晶片貸款。

Conning結構型商品主管Michael Nowakowski認為，本金攤還、較低貸款成數，以及GPU占比不持續增加，是讓投資人較安心的重要條件。相較全數由GPU融資組成的交易，他對這類多元資產池的疑慮較小。他的條件針對擔保資產組成與還款結構，而不只是是否含有AI相關資產。

日本央行副總裁內田真一週一就AI建設對利率的影響提出新評估。他表示，AI初期是一項龐大的正向需求衝擊，增加經濟活動與物價壓力。科技股上漲可能放鬆金融條件，大量科技債券發行則可能推升較長期殖利率、收緊金融條件。其後生產力改善與資本增加，可能改變中性實質利率，但整體方向仍不確定。

內田也警告，AI可能使部分知識型技能失去用途、擴大不平等，有科技技能與調整彈性的人可能獲益較多。這些影響使「投資增強必然代表中性利率永久升高」的推論更加複雜，也為融資討論加入具名的政策觀點，卻未對長期利率影響作出定論。

晶片基礎設施以外，工業收購融資仍然活躍。銀行開始推介等值€47億的貸款，支應Bain Capital收購福斯汽車重型柴油引擎業務Everllence的控制股權。歐元與美元貸款各為等值€23.5億，初步加碼幅度分別為3.5與3.75個百分點，兩者發行價格皆為面額的99.5%。

Moody’s給予B1評等，估計交易後槓桿為獲利的6.4倍，警告較高融資成本讓營運表現不如預期時的承受空間有限。Bain於6月同意購入51%股權，預計交易為福斯帶來約€74億收入。Barclays與Goldman Sachs名列實體簿記管理人，投資人下單截止日為10月13日。週一也有一筆$10.5億貸款開始推介，支應收購Flow Control Holdings的控制股權，併購持續帶來槓桿融資需求。

Schneider Electric宣布更大的企業投資承諾，以全現金約$226億收購波士頓工業軟體公司PTC，為其史上最大收購，較PTC上一個收盤股價溢價逾40%。市場擔心交易規模與龐大融資，Schneider股價下跌，但JPMorgan與Citi分析師認為，交易有助於強化工業自動化地位。PTC將帶來用於汽車、航太與醫療科技產品設計、建造及管理的工程軟體。

今年歐洲工業收購金額已成長至逾三倍，全球工業併購成長則不到15%；非美國買方收購美國標的的金額超過$2,000億，為2021年以來最高。在較高殖利率未能阻止策略買方追求軟體、自動化與AI能力之際，Schneider的新承諾再添收購資金需求。

能源安全也帶來潛在融資需求。Bharat Petroleum準備分數批發行最高$30億的國際債券，主要支應其對巴西SEAP-I離岸計畫的$28億出資，並為明年到期債務再融資。公司上月已在倫敦、杜拜與新加坡進行投資人路演。旗下Bharat PetroResources持有BM-SEAL-11區域40%權益，該區由Petrobras營運。

SEAP-I全面營運後，設計每日產油120,000桶、處理天然氣1,000萬立方公尺，目標2030年開始產油、2031年出口天然氣。印度原油近90%、天然氣約一半仰賴進口，這筆擬議借款將支應長期能源來源多元化計畫。今年印度向巴西採購的原油，較2025年水準增加逾一倍，巴西已成為其第五大供應國。

美國副總統范斯週一提出另一項、尚較不確定的能源投資承諾。他說阿拉斯加LNG管線將推進，但承認與南韓的細節仍待協商。首爾方面表示，雖然計畫被納入川普宣布的$2,000億對美投資架構，仍未定案。范斯以美國天然氣需求強勁作為信心依據。

## 再融資延後與寬頻業者債券重挫，信用表現分化

週一，美國投資級與高收益債整體利差小幅收窄，硬通貨新興市場債利差則明顯收窄，信用溢價改善減輕美債殖利率上升對部分證券的影響。LQD經配息調整後的單日報酬持平，HYG上漲0.09%，EMB上漲0.22%，與長天期政府債券下跌形成對比。

JPMorgan由Nathaniel Rosenbaum領軍的策略團隊，在週五首度發表、週一進一步披露的報告中，對第四季持正面看法。他們預測JULI投資級利差由週五的0.96個百分點降至0.85個百分點，約相當於彭博美國企業債利差由週五的0.82個百分點降至0.73個百分點。判斷依據是企業獲利強勁、利率波動減弱，以及殖利率穩定後，發行量與國內外需求的平衡改善。

JPMorgan預估今年剩餘時間發行量約$3,050億，第四季將依一般季節規律，成為發行最少的一季。大型雲端業者可能再發行$500億債券，但策略師認為，相較這些科技公司今年已完成的全球發行量，這個金額不大。企業債可望優於美債的預測，取決於基本面與供給減少；各借款人對高融資成本的敏感度仍有差異。

Virgin Media O2立即成為整體信用市場平靜之外的例外。週一其美國高收益債跌至歷史低點，Virgin Media Finance票息5%的債券每1美元面額下跌8美分，最低成交至42美分；Vmed O2 UK Financing於2032年到期的歐元債，每1歐元面額下跌6歐分至70.5歐分。其美元債是美國高收益市場當日跌幅最大的債券。

英國競爭與市場管理局週五對Nexfibre擬以£20億與Netomnia合併提出初步反對意見，引發這波下跌。Virgin Media的股東Liberty Global與Telefónica，也是Nexfibre三名股東中的兩名。合併原本將擴大Virgin Media網路覆蓋、支持轉型；彭博行業研究分析師Erhan Gurses表示，計畫仰賴£9.5億的淨現金挹注。若遭阻擋，Virgin Media可能必須增加自有光纖網路升級支出，雖可部分透過省下批發費用抵銷。

週一BT宣布已收購TalkTalk，擴大這家主要競爭對手的客戶群，再添競爭威脅。Ironshield分析師Isharsimran Sawhney將Virgin Media的困境歸因於競爭、營運表現不佳、自由現金流偏弱，以及龐大資本支出需求，這些因素都限制債務減少。公司公布6月底對第三方債務與租賃義務約£225億，折合$290億。最近一筆到期債務在2029年，因此這次債券重估聚焦於降低槓桿的路徑，而非迫在眉睫的還款。

美國地方政府發行人較有餘裕延後借款，代價則是原訂再融資節省無法實現。FHN Financial公共融資主管Ajay Thomas估計，約$60億的借新還舊交易暫停或延後，借款人等待殖利率下降。30年期地方政府債指標殖利率先升至約5.26%，為至少2011年以來最高，週一回落至約5.12%，但仍使部分再融資計畫不具經濟效益。

新澤西州Transportation Trust Fund Authority原訂10月1日進行約$17億的借新還舊發行，最終未定價。該機構6月底未償債務為$178億，負責道路、橋梁與大眾運輸融資，包括New Jersey Transit。PNC公共融資主管Samantha Funk表示，費城學區原定本週進行的$4.5億再融資，也改為逐日視情況安排。

紐約Metropolitan Transportation Authority希望本月借新還舊$10億，仍須視市場情況而定。金融服務副主管Olga Chernat在9月底表示，更大的疑慮是未來新債成本，將納入11月財務計畫。若再融資目的是節省利息，就可以等待；新資本支出承諾則在高利率持續時面對不同限制。

貸款人撤回支持後，鐵礦砂交易商Radiant World的壓力也延伸至日常營運。法院指定管理人接管公司營運之際，其新加坡、中國與歐洲員工表示，9月薪資未依往常月底時程入帳。債權人質疑公司以涉嫌偽造文件取得融資，銀行此前已停止提供資金。

## 從巴西到烏克蘭，主權市場走勢分歧

巴西大選帶來當日最強烈的固定收益市場反應之一。Flávio Bolsonaro在週日首輪投票獲約47%選票，領先總統魯拉的約45%，出乎普遍預期魯拉領先的投資人意料。兩人將於10月25日進入第二輪投票。右翼在州長、眾議院與參議院選舉中也有強勁表現，改變市場對財政方案落實可能性的看法。

利率交換合約利率下跌逾100個基點，巴西里爾升值近5%，Ibovespa上漲8%至歷史新高。彭博週一報導中，巴西美元債是新興市場表現最佳的債券。投資人認為，抑制支出、建立可信財政約束並容許利率下降的機率提高，而非只期待一位缺乏立法支持的新總統上任。

UBS策略師Alejo Czerwonko與Luciano Telo在選後，將更深入且持久的財政調整列為基本情境。UBS財富管理經濟學家Solange Srour表示，若出現可信的財政整頓訊號，可能帶動長天期債券上漲，利差最多收窄250個基點。利率交換走勢已反映市場大幅重新評估財政前景，但Bolsonaro尚未提出詳細經濟方案，投資人對結果的熱情，與實際削減支出的工作仍是兩回事。

其他市場在美元走強、歐洲主權疑慮下，結果較不利。南非10年期殖利率升至六個月高點，蘭特走弱。開發中市場科技股則提供支撐，台積電因可能與馬斯克的Terafab合作而上漲逾3%。在已開發市場融資成本走高的全球背景下，巴西財政樂觀帶來的支撐格外突出。

土耳其新公布的通膨，提供另一條利率下降的可能路徑。消費者物價年增率連續四個月放緩，由31.5%降至29.7%，低於彭博調查中位數30.3%；月增率1.84%，與8月相同，低於另一項2.28%預期。運輸、教育與住房是月增幅的主要貢獻項目。2年期里拉債殖利率下降36個基點至39.49%，銀行股一度上漲2.8%。

BBVA的Tufan Comert認為，整體與核心通膨改善，強化10月22日會議降息的理由，但能源價格與地緣政治不確定性，要求對降息速度保持謹慎。MUFG Turkey的Onur Ilgen持相反看法，預期若能源成本未顯著下降，10月不會行動。基金危機後流動性受抑，正在冷卻活動與需求，但若投資人尋求外幣，里拉壓力可能抵銷通膨降溫。這次低於預期的通膨，給主張寬鬆者新的支持，卻未消除分歧。

S&P週五維持羅馬尼亞BBB-評等、未降至投資級以下，帶動其資產上漲。週一國內10年期殖利率下降12個基點至7.24%，比一週前低約40個基點。財政部售出2028年到期債券RON5.32億，折合$1.12億，超過目標，也是9月初以來首次成功達成預定規模的標售。布加勒斯特股市指標上漲2.9%，列伊升值0.1%，約為每歐元5.334列伊。

S&P仍維持負向展望，警告政治動盪若持續，可能妨礙未來兩年削減赤字。Raiffeisen經濟學家Stephan Imre表示，原訂年度評等檢視如今已完成，焦點轉向2027年預算的財政整頓，但第四季仍可能有非例行評等行動。兩次成立完整政府的嘗試失敗後，總統Nicușor Dan計畫再與主流政黨會談，並可能另提名一位總理。評等決定改善了融資，組閣問題卻仍未解決。

印度主權殖利率曲線面對相反的政策方向。ICBC財資主管Alok Sharma預期，隨印度央行回收流動性、使隔夜利率更接近附買回政策利率，5年與10年期利差可能收窄至10個基點左右。若隔夜利率顯著高於政策利率，曲線可能持平或略呈倒掛。ICICI Securities Primary Dealership認為，若緊縮仍積極，5年期殖利率可能由6.94%升向7%。這些新的曲線預測指出，已在進行的流動性回收可能造成哪些利率壓力。

日本9月服務業終值顯示，擴張放緩但勞動需求持續。指數由52.5降至51.3，低於51.6初值；綜合指數由53.5降至52.3，為5月以來最低。新訂單連續二十七個月增加，但增速減慢；新出口業務降幅為2021年1月以來第二大。就業連續十三個月增加，增速為2月以來最快，未完成訂單增幅達七個月高點。

日本投入成本通膨降至六個月低點，仍處於歷史偏高水準，來源包括原物料、原油、勞動與食品，售價通膨也放緩。加拿大調查顯示更弱的需求：服務業活動指數由46.8升至48.3，仍連續四個月萎縮；綜合指數由47.8升至48.7，仍低於50。新業務指數48.5，連續五個月萎縮，出口弱勢也加深。

加拿大投入價格指數由61.7升至62.2，未來活動預期則由56.4升至61.4，為五個月高點。S&P Global經濟學家Paul Smith將不確定性、出口下降與營運成本上升，連結到關稅與伊朗戰爭。與美國及歐元區不同，加拿大面對的是實際萎縮與成本上升並存，即使信心回升，成長與通膨之間的取捨仍較不利。

烏克蘭面對更急迫的融資緊縮。路透報導，這是2022年全面入侵以來最嚴重的預算危機，今年融資缺口$560億，約占GDP四分之一，其中$270億用於軍事支出。政府凍結非必要支出，包括受損建築與基礎設施重建，優先支應國防、公部門薪資與退休金。

不計西方直接軍援，每日作戰成本已由兩年前約$1.4億升至$1.9億。今年前九個月國防支出逾$440億，稅收則約$420億。政府估計，俄羅斯攻擊在這段期間造成逾UAH495億、約$11億的稅收損失，年底可能達UAH700億。

稅務與反貪腐立法延遲，阻礙數十億歐元外國貸款撥付。總理Sergii Koretskyi表示，今年$295億援助面臨風險。烏克蘭正討論提前取得原訂明年撥付的歐盟€900億貸款，但知情人士警告，將資金提前，可能把壓力移至2027年。明年擬議國防預算在未計直接軍援前達創紀錄的$1,100億，財政部長Sergii Marchenko估計，未有資金支應的缺口超過$320億。

收入基礎受損，使融資問題更嚴重。工廠、倉庫、港口與鐵路遭攻擊，受影響的鋼鐵生產在戰前約占產出十分之一。9月穀物出口年減36.6%，經濟部長Oleksandr Kravchenko表示，每年約$400億出口收入面臨風險。經濟學家預期今年成長僅0.5%至1.5%，低於2025年的1.8%。加快官方融資可支應眼前付款，但改革條件與生產能力遭破壞，仍是各自存在的限制。

## 後續市場觀察

美國財政部本輪標售從10月6日開始，紐約時間下午1時發行$580億3年期公債，稍後本週還有10年與30年期標售。長天期債券再度下跌後，接近數十年高點的殖利率能否吸引足夠需求，將由長天期標售檢驗。另一項新的技術面警告是，長端殖利率若繼續上升，可能改變期貨避險所依據的可交割債券，標售反應因而更加重要。

BNP Paribas策略師Guneet Dhingra、Sebastian Mauleon與Vincent Zhou警告，若最便宜可交割券轉向更長天期，可能迫使期貨部位進一步調整。目前長債期貨合約的最便宜可交割券，是票息2.5%、2045年2月到期的美債；彭博情境分析顯示，30年期殖利率接近6%時，可能轉向2050年到期券。若要維持投資組合存續期間不變，期貨多頭須賣出，空頭須買回，因此市場淨影響取決於部位與調整時點。

9月29日部位資料顯示，資產管理機構一週內削減近100,000口超長債期貨淨多單，同週30年期殖利率從5.28%升至最高5.62%。彭博估計，減少的風險曝險約為每基點$1,500萬，相當於$110億目前的長天期公債。SMBC的Monty Gandhi表示，超長債合約已轉向存續期間較長的可交割券，長債合約則仍面對存續期間延長風險。BMO Asset Management的Earl Davis另預測，長債殖利率可能本月就達6%，因波動可能加劇賣壓。上述情境與預測，都不是自動觸發干預的門檻。

10月6日紐約時間上午8時15分，ADP將公布每週就業數據，前值20,000人。週一服務業招聘改善後，這項數據將提供新的招募觀察。上午8時30分公布8月貿易數據，共識預期逆差由$886億擴大至$1,020億。進出口組成將有助於判斷，強勁內需是否伴隨更大的外部拖累，而非各項活動都同步擴張。

John Williams、Michelle Bowman與Lorie Logan預定10月6日，分別於紐約時間上午9時05分、上午10時45分與晚間7時發表談話。服務業成本壓力與較長期實質殖利率上升後，他們的新評估將格外重要。週一利率市場報導中的利率交換定價，顯示聯準會10月升息機率約25%，並已完全反映12月前升息25個基點。9月會議紀錄週三公布，將說明已實施升息的理由，官員談話則可回應較新的資訊。

週三印度央行決策，市場預期附買回政策利率上升25個基點至5.50%。利率決定與流動性吸收指引，對曲線預測同樣重要：政策利率上升但未有效傳導至隔夜市場，與融資條件收緊且利率進一步上升，是不同情況。在歐洲，德國11月1日儲氣期限將近，給Nagel的供給警告一個具體時間範圍。若服務業訂單仍具韌性、價格又繼續加速，ECB仍受限制，即使主權壓力使另行採取資產負債表措施的理由增強。

企業融資需求有明確期限。Everllence貸款10月13日截止下單，Volta承諾出資截止日為10月14日，Stonebriar設備ABS也預計10月14日交割。市場反應將顯示，投資人對不同條件的工業槓桿、未評等AI貸款與多元GPU擔保資產的吸收意願。對Virgin Media O2而言，競爭審查與BT收購TalkTalk的後果，比整體高收益市場轉強更重要；地方政府借款人則可能在殖利率降到足以恢復再融資節省時，啟動目前逐日等待的交易。

巴西10月25日第二輪投票，意味這波急漲仍取決於選舉結果與可信的財政細節。土耳其10月22日會議，面對通膨讀數下降，但能源與匯率風險持續。烏克蘭要求加快歐洲融資，其眼前考驗不同：能否在支出需求迫使預算其他項目進一步削減前，協調好撥款時程與改革條件。

週二另行進行的亞洲早盤，澳洲與紐西蘭公債隨美國長端賣壓下跌。澳洲10年期殖利率上升6個基點至5.39%，Nasdaq 100期貨則上漲約0.2%。較晚的交易延續債券與科技股主導股市的分歧；週一已完成的美國交易日，主調仍是油價轉弱、信用市場轉強，卻未阻止長期實質殖利率上升。

overall_summary.session_narrative:
10月5日長天期美債下跌，9月服務業調查顯示需求仍具韌性、招聘改善，企業成本持續上升。ISM活動指數降至54.9，但支付價格升至74.0，為2022年7月以來最高；S&P Global服務業活動指數達58.8，擴張力道為2021年7月以來最強。整體經濟招聘放緩，尚未使需求充分降溫到足以緩解價格設定壓力。

10年期與30年期美債殖利率分別上升3.4與4.3個基點，至5.307%與5.664%，2年期下降1.4個基點至4.813%；2年與10年期利差擴大4.8個基點至49.4個基點。10年期實質殖利率上升3.5個基點至2.944%，損益兩平通膨率小降0.1個基點至2.363%，名目殖利率升幅主要來自實質借款成本提高。油價下跌約2%，股票上漲，美國投資級與高收益債利差小幅收窄，硬通貨新興市場債利差明顯收窄，仍未能阻止長天期美債賣壓。

法國財政壓力更清楚地反映在銀行信用，法國興業銀行的違約保障成本超過德意志銀行同類保障，歐元跌至17個月低點。歐元區服務業活動韌性與新一波能源壓力，使ECB回應更複雜。巴西走向相反：Flávio Bolsonaro意外在首輪大選領先，財政整頓希望帶動利率交換利率下跌逾100個基點，但其詳細經濟方案尚未確立。

借款持續，條件卻愈來愈分化。Volta的$50億AI貸款以約11%殖利率推介，GPU曝險也進入多元設備證券化。地方政府借款人延後約$60億再融資；監管阻礙與競爭加劇威脅降低槓桿，Virgin Media O2債券重挫。本週較長天期美債標售，將檢驗長期融資成本再度上升後的需求。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Long-dated Treasuries lost ground on October 5 as fresh evidence of strong services demand and rising business costs sustained the pressure on borrowing rates. The 10-year Treasury yield rose 3.4 basis points to 5.307% and the 30-year yield rose 4.3 basis points to 5.664%, while the two-year fell 1.4 basis points to 4.813%. September's services surveys showed that slower recruitment across the economy had not extinguished demand or relieved capacity constraints. ISM's prices measure reached its highest since July 2022, and S&P Global reported its strongest services expansion since July 2021.

The selloff was concentrated beyond the immediate policy horizon. The 10-year real yield rose 3.5 basis points against a 3.4-basis-point rise in the nominal yield, with the 0.1-basis-point decline in inflation compensation providing a small offset. Oil fell roughly 2%, equities advanced and U.S. corporate spreads tightened modestly. Those counterforces did not prevent longer borrowing rates from rising: the session combined resilient activity with a market still demanding more compensation to supply long-term capital.

Europe's fiscal strains acquired a more visible banking and currency dimension. French bank default protection became more expensive than comparable protection for major European peers, the euro touched a 17-month low, and Spain called an early election. ECB officials continued to emphasize inflation control while distinguishing renewed energy pressure from a lasting change in wages and price-setting. Elsewhere, Brazil supplied a sharp contrast: an unexpected first-round election lead for Flávio Bolsonaro sent swap rates tumbling as investors reassessed the prospects for fiscal consolidation.

Borrowing continued despite expensive money, but its terms and urgency increasingly separated issuers. A $5 billion AI infrastructure loan was marketed at an approximately 11% yield, while equipment securitizations began carrying meaningful GPU exposure. Municipal borrowers postponed refinancing rather than surrender the savings they sought, and Virgin Media O2's bonds plunged as an obstacle to broadband consolidation threatened its deleveraging plans.

## Services Demand Keeps Pressure on Long Treasuries

The September ISM services index eased to 54.9 from 55.4, a modest slowdown that left activity expanding for a twenty-seventh consecutive month. The reading was below the 55.2 consensus in Reuters' survey and the separate 55 expectation recorded by Trading Economics. Thirteen industries reported growth and four contracted, including mining and construction. The larger part of the economy was still expanding across a broad group of businesses rather than relying solely on the technology investment boom.

Business activity fell to 56.5 from 61.7, below the 61.5 expectation, and new orders declined to 59.8 from 60.9 against a 60.3 forecast. But employment returned to expansion at 50.1 after 47.8, exceeding the expected 48 and ending two months of contraction. That combination offered a different labor observation from Friday's weak payroll recruitment: services firms collectively reported an improvement in hiring even as the pace of output growth moderated.

Cost and delivery pressures became more pronounced. Prices paid increased to 74.0 from 72.6, above the 72.9 forecast and the sixth reading above 70 in seven months. Respondents identified increases in copper, diesel, steel, petroleum-related products and memory products. The supplier-deliveries index rose to 53.2 from 51.3, extending a twenty-two-month run of slower deliveries. Backlogs reached 56.6, their highest since July 2022, and increased for an eighth month.

Steve Miller, chairman of ISM's Services Business Survey Committee, said tariffs and fuel costs were the supply-chain problems businesses mentioned most frequently. Fuel costs were cited about twice as often as any other individual problem. Export orders, meanwhile, fell below 50 for the first time in eight months. Domestic demand was sustaining activity while external orders weakened and the cost of serving customers rose. Some firms also described organizational restructuring and the use of AI tools to improve efficiency.

S&P Global's separate final services survey showed a stronger acceleration. Its index reached 58.8, up from August's 56.5 and slightly above both the 58.7 flash estimate and consensus. Expansion continued for a sixth month and was the strongest since July 2021. Technology led, but consumer businesses, industrials and healthcare also accelerated. The final composite index rose to 58.4 from 56.0, matching expectations.

New orders in the S&P survey grew at their fastest pace in more than four years, supported by strong domestic demand. Employment increased for a third month, with hiring the fastest since June 2022. Backlogs accumulated for a nineteenth consecutive month as orders outpaced capacity. Input costs rose at their strongest rate since November 2022, reflecting gas and labor costs, while output-charge inflation was the second-highest in just over a year. Business confidence reached a one-year high.

The surveys disagreed on the change in headline activity, but their detail did not point to a generalized weakening of services demand. Both showed growing orders, renewed or accelerating hiring, backlogs and substantial cost pressure. For the Fed, the consequential distinction is between an economy adding fewer workers overall and one in which demand has cooled enough to ease the price-setting environment. Monday's releases gave more evidence for the former than the latter.

BMO Capital Markets strategist Vail Hartman judged the ISM report consistent with mounting inflation pressure and strong nominal growth, reinforcing the forces behind the recent bond selloff. Bloomberg's intraday Treasury account recorded benchmark 10- and 30-year yields rising at least 7 basis points to 5.34% and 5.70%, their highest levels since 2002. For October 5, the daily yields stood at 5.307% for the 10-year and 5.664% for the long bond.

The daily yield curve steepened as the front end rallied and longer maturities sold off. The five-year edged up 0.4 basis points to 5.058%, and the 2s10s spread widened 4.8 basis points to 49.4. The 2s30s spread widened 5.7 basis points to 85.1. Over the week, the two-year was down 11.9 basis points while the 10-year was up 7.0 and the 30-year up 11.6; 2s10s had widened 18.9 basis points. The differing directions show how relief over the immediate policy outlook had failed to carry through to long-term financing.

At 10 years, the real yield rose 3.5 basis points to 2.944%, while breakeven inflation slipped 0.1 basis points to 2.363%. The month's comparison was similarly dominated by real rates: the nominal yield was up 52.4 basis points, the real yield up 51.4 and the breakeven up 1.0. Renewed survey inflation pressure helped explain why bonds found little reassurance in slower headline ISM activity, but the market's longer-term inflation compensation was broadly flat, with a slight decline on the day. Higher real borrowing costs accounted for most of the observed nominal yield rise.

Oil supplied some relief. WTI fell 2.03% to $89.26 a barrel and Brent declined 1.97% to $100.24 at the fixed-income close. Brent nevertheless remained 8.58% above its month-earlier level. President Donald Trump was preparing to relax restrictions on the use of a tax-exempt form of diesel in a further attempt to reduce fuel costs. The proposal addressed a current source of business pressure while the ISM survey was registering the costs already reaching respondents.

Equities held up better than duration. The S&P 500 gained 0.66% to 7,773.95, close to a record, and the Nasdaq 100 rose 0.87% to a new peak at 31,076.44. Morgan Stanley Wealth Management's Lisa Shalett attributed the relative calm to accelerating growth and the AI boom's limited sensitivity to rates. Nationwide's Mark Hackett pointed to earnings growth and improving margins as a counterweight to increasingly punitive financing costs.

The strength was narrower beneath the indices. Bloomberg's market analysis reported nearly 60% of S&P 500 constituents below their 200-day moving averages and about 75% below their 50-day averages. Goldman Sachs prime-brokerage data showed hedge funds spending much of September adding shorts and hedges rather than cutting their long positions. The resulting concentration allowed the main indices to advance while businesses more exposed to financing and energy costs remained under pressure.

A separate Monday analysis put the MOVE Treasury-options volatility index around 108, almost seven times the contemporaneous VIX reading and the widest ratio since late 2024. The VIX subsequently stood at 15.52 in the day's market observations. The contrast exposed different assessments of risk across bonds and equities without requiring a fall in current corporate profits. The Dollar Index gained 0.17% to 102.102, while gold futures edged up 0.15% to $4,168.40 an ounce.

## French Risk Spreads Into Banks as ECB Weighs Energy Pressure

French sovereign stress became more clearly visible in the relative pricing of bank credit. On Monday, five-year protection on EUR10 million of Societe Generale bail-in senior debt cost EUR103,000 annually, about EUR16,500 more than comparable Deutsche Bank protection. The costs had been equal in late August. BNP Paribas and Credit Agricole default-protection premiums were also well above those of major lenders in the UK, Germany, Switzerland and Spain.

The difference brings the sovereign concern into bank funding through two routes: lenders' holdings of government bonds and their exposure to economic policies affecting borrowers. ING strategists Jeroen van den Broek and Timothy Rahill said higher rates, renewed fiscal concern and uncertainty had broken the recent calm in euro credit, with the largest weakness in French risk and some spillover into peripheral markets. The newly measured bank gap added a concrete credit-market development to the already established deterioration in French government bonds.

OATs again lagged bunds. In Bloomberg's Monday trading account, the French-German 10-year spread widened 10 basis points to 150, while longer-dated French and Italian securities underperformed German equivalents. The move renewed pressure within the session rather than establishing another record beyond the extremes reached the previous week. Germany continued to attract the safer part of the region's government-bond demand.

The currency adjustment was more conspicuous. The euro fell as much as 0.8% to $1.1161, its weakest since May 2025, as Asian fast-money funds sold it for dollars and the move triggered additional options-related selling. ING's Chris Turner interpreted weakness against several major currencies as a larger fiscal-risk premium and saw a risk of a further move toward $1.10. Euro risk reversals were near their most bearish levels since March 2025, although below the extremes associated with earlier episodes of outright panic.

Spain added a new political event. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez called an election for November 29 after his minority government failed to pass housing legislation intended to address a worsening affordability crisis. The opposition People's Party led polls and could seek a coalition with far-right Vox; the parties already govern together in four regions, including Andalusia. Credit Agricole's Valentin Marinov said the Spanish headlines were less influential for the euro than France's problems, but did not help its position.

New estimates of the Japanese investor base showed why French yields alone might not rebuild overseas demand. Bloomberg calculated that Japanese investors held JPY23 trillion, or $145 billion, of French bonds in July. France accounted for 6.6% of their overseas debt holdings and was their largest euro-area overweight relative to the Bloomberg Global Aggregate Index. Holdings had fallen 2.5% since the end of last year.

The recent selloff left the French 10-year yield about 40 basis points above Japan's on a currency-hedged basis. Mizuho's Masayuki Nakajima argued that the pickup could still be insufficient given uncertainty over France's fiscal trajectory and hedging costs. Rising domestic Japanese yields make repatriation more attractive, while a large existing overweight means foreign demand cannot be assessed from the nominal French yield in isolation. Fivestar Asset Management's Hideo Shimomura warned that the French yield could reach 7% if the ECB left the situation unchecked.

Former ECB Executive Board member Lorenzo Bini Smaghi made a fresh public case for suspending bond runoff in a Financial Times opinion article Monday. He argued that interest rates should remain the main policy instrument and balance-sheet changes a secondary one, with quantitative tightening paused until conditions stabilized and its financial-market effects were better understood. His recommendation extended the debate over reinvestment; it was not an ECB decision or a promise to cap French spreads.

The broader intervention problem drew a warning from BIS General Manager Pablo Hernandez de Cos. Government debt near postwar highs and persistently large deficits, he said Monday, make it harder for central banks to distinguish market dysfunction from investors' reasonable repricing of fiscal risk. A response needed to protect financial stability or monetary transmission could nevertheless be perceived as fiscal assistance.

Hernandez de Cos also emphasized the government-bond holdings of hedge funds, pension funds and asset managers, whose leverage and reliance on market funding can amplify volatility during stress. He cited the 2020 U.S. dash for cash and the 2022 gilt crisis, describing the Bank of England's limited-duration purchases as one possible template. Such limits might be less credible in a larger or more persistent crisis, he warned. Faster digital finance, social media, stablecoins and AI could accelerate future pressure, while central-bank swap lines remained important for acute global liquidity needs.

The ECB's current inflation assessment offered no simple permission to ease. Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel said Monday that upside risks dominated, while stressing that there were still no clear signs of the shock feeding broadly into wage and price-setting. Longer-term market and expert expectations remained consistent with the 2% target. He did not endorse a particular market-implied timetable for increases and called for flexibility and meeting-by-meeting decisions.

His energy warning became more specific in Germany. Gas storage was about 59% full, the lowest seasonal level in records beginning in 2009, against an EU average of 72%. Operators warned that the current injection pace made the legal target of about 70% by November 1 nearly impossible to meet. The government had instructed state-owned SEFE to purchase and store gas in the coming weeks after relying largely on utilities and traders earlier in the season.

The Iran war had pushed near-term gas prices above winter prices, undermining the commercial incentive to store fuel. Nagel criticized the slow replenishment after the previous winter and warned that larger, more expensive winter purchases could add to inflation. Damage to refining capacity was also raising product prices, while drought, wildfires and fertilizer shortages created additional food-price risks. These were concrete supply constraints behind his assessment, not a claim that a generalized wage-price response had already begun.

ECB Chief Economist Philip Lane separately advocated a measured response as officials assessed a second wave of energy pressure. The economy had proved unexpectedly resilient to the first wave, he said, but renewed costs could weigh more heavily on both activity and inflation. Duration, intensity and pass-through mattered alongside fiscal conditions, AI and overall financing conditions. Lane judged Europe's AI investment still too small to create significant wage pressure through data-center construction, distinguishing its present macroeconomic scale from the U.S. buildout.

Monday's final euro-area PMIs supported the resilience side of that judgment. The services index rose to 53.0 from 51.6, matching its flash reading and reaching a ten-month high. The composite increased to 53.1 from 52.0, its highest since April 2023, making Q3 the strongest quarter since Q2 2022. S&P Global's Chris Williamson estimated that the survey corresponded to GDP growth of around 0.4% quarter on quarter.

Spain led activity, followed by Ireland; Germany's recovery accelerated while Italy and France grew modestly. Services export orders ended thirty-nine months of contraction, and combined manufacturing and services orders rose at their fastest pace in forty-one months. Overseas demand increased at its strongest rate in more than four and a half years. Employment gains weakened as slower services hiring offset a small manufacturing improvement, but input and output prices both accelerated to four-month highs. The combination left the ECB confronting renewed price pressure in an economy not yet displaying the broad demand weakness that might readily offset it.

## AI Borrowing Reaches Loans and Equipment Securitizations

JPMorgan began marketing a $5 billion leveraged loan for Volta Infrastructure Holdings at an approximately 11% yield, setting out an expensive financing structure for a new AI cloud business. Initial terms were 6.25-6.5 percentage points over the benchmark rate and a price of 97-98 cents on the dollar. The approximately 11% all-in yield reflected those margins, discounts and current benchmark rates; the margin itself was not the total cost of the debt.

The financing combines chips and a data-center lease rather than funding a single equipment purchase. A $3.7 billion tranche would buy about 36,000 Nvidia GPUs. A further $1.3 billion would cash-collateralize a letter of credit supporting lease payments to Bitdeer Technologies, which is partnering with Volta on a Norwegian data-center complex. Anthropic has signed a six-year agreement for compute capacity at the site, according to people familiar with the arrangement.

Lenders must purchase portions of both tranches through a strip structure, and the loans fully amortize over time. The borrower is the special-purpose entity Volta Tydal Holdings. The debt is unrated, an unusual feature that typically prevents CLOs, the leveraged-loan market's largest buyer group, from purchasing it. A lender call took place at 11 a.m. New York time Monday, with commitments due October 14.

Volta was founded this year by former Brookfield infrastructure executives Ricard Boada and Sofia Gumuzio. Its terms highlight the funding distinction between newer cloud operators and businesses able to borrow with investment-grade corporate support. Previous neocloud financings had carried lower costs; this package also includes data-center-related financing alongside the chip loan. Anthropic's capacity contract supplies a customer commitment, while the loan's price, amortization and restricted buyer base define the capital required to deliver it.

GPU exposure is also entering equipment-backed bonds. Stonebriar Commercial Finance is selling around $869 million of ABS with GPU loans representing approximately 15% of collateral. The transaction is expected to be marketed this week and settle October 14. Expected ratings range from AAA to BBB-, with the shortest-lived securities expected to receive the highest short-term ratings, and the Rule 144A offering is directed to qualified institutional investors.

The collateral is not exclusively AI hardware. Computer and IT infrastructure is the largest category, alongside oil and gas equipment, manufacturing assets, corporate aircraft and marine assets. Wingspire Equipment Finance raised more than $407 million through an equipment-loan and lease securitization late last month, with GPUs accounting for about 20% of its pool; its institutional offering included AAA-rated securities. The newly disclosed proportions show AI hardware financing entering diversified equipment pools rather than remaining confined to dedicated chip loans.

Conning's structured-products head Michael Nowakowski regarded amortizing loans, lower loan-to-value ratios and a GPU share that did not keep rising as important conditions for comfort. He was less concerned about such diversified pools than about transactions consisting entirely of GPU financing. His qualification concerns the composition and repayment structure of the collateral, not simply the presence of an AI-related asset.

The buildout's effect on interest rates also drew a fresh central-bank assessment. BOJ Deputy Governor Shinichi Uchida said Monday that AI first acts as a large positive demand shock, raising pressure on activity and prices. Higher technology stock prices can loosen financial conditions, while substantial tech bond issuance raises longer-term yields and tightens them. Productivity improvements and additional capital could subsequently alter the neutral real interest rate, but the overall direction remained uncertain.

Uchida also warned that AI could make some intellectual skills obsolete and widen inequality, with larger benefits accruing to people who have technological skills and flexibility. Those effects complicate an inference that stronger investment necessarily means a permanently higher neutral rate. His assessment added a named policy perspective to the financing debate while leaving the long-term rate implication unresolved.

Industrial acquisition borrowing remained active outside chip infrastructure. Banks launched EUR4.7 billion-equivalent of loans for Bain Capital's purchase of a controlling stake in Volkswagen's Everllence heavy diesel-engine business. The package comprises EUR2.35 billion-equivalent each in euro and dollar loans. Initial margins were 3.5 percentage points for the euro financing and 3.75 for the dollar financing, with both offered at 99.5% of face value.

Moody's assigned B1 ratings and estimated post-transaction leverage at 6.4 times earnings, warning that higher financing costs left limited room for operating underperformance. Bain agreed in June to buy 51%, with the transaction expected to generate about EUR7.4 billion of proceeds for Volkswagen. Barclays and Goldman Sachs are among the physical bookrunners, and investors have until October 13 to place orders. Monday also brought a $1.05 billion loan launch for the purchase of a controlling stake in Flow Control Holdings, continuing the acquisition-led demand for leveraged financing.

Schneider Electric announced a much larger corporate commitment: an all-cash purchase of Boston-based industrial software company PTC for about $22.6 billion, its biggest acquisition. The premium exceeded 40% over PTC's last closing share price. Schneider shares fell amid concern over the transaction's size and heavy financing, although JPMorgan and Citi analysts saw an opportunity to strengthen its industrial-automation position. PTC adds engineering software used to design, build and manage products across automotive, aerospace and medical technology.

The agreement comes as the value of European industrial acquisitions has more than tripled this year, compared with growth of less than 15% for industrial M&A globally. Acquisitions of U.S. targets by non-U.S. buyers have exceeded $200 billion, the largest tally since 2021. Schneider's new commitment adds to demand for acquisition capital at a time when higher yields have not stopped strategic buyers from pursuing software, automation and AI capabilities.

Energy security supplied another prospective funding need. Bharat Petroleum is preparing an international bond sale of as much as $3 billion in several tranches, largely to support its $2.8 billion contribution to Brazil's SEAP-I offshore project and refinance debt due next year. It held investor roadshows in London, Dubai and Singapore last month. Subsidiary Bharat PetroResources owns 40% of the BM-SEAL-11 area, operated by Petrobras.

SEAP-I is designed to produce 120,000 barrels of oil daily and process 10 million cubic meters of gas a day when fully operational. Oil output is targeted for 2030 and gas exports for 2031. The prospective borrowing funds a long-dated diversification project, with India importing almost 90% of its crude and around half its gas. Its crude purchases from Brazil have more than doubled from 2025 levels this year, making Brazil its fifth-largest supplier.

U.S. Vice President JD Vance offered a different, less settled energy-investment commitment Monday. He said the Alaska LNG pipeline would proceed but acknowledged that details with South Korea remained to be negotiated. Seoul has said the project is not finalized despite its inclusion in Trump's announcement of a $200 billion U.S. investment framework. Vance cited strong U.S. gas demand as grounds for confidence.

## Refinancing Delays and Broadband Losses Divide Credit

Broad U.S. investment-grade and high-yield spreads tightened modestly Monday, while hard-currency emerging-market spreads tightened noticeably. The improvement in credit premiums softened the effect of higher Treasury yields on some securities. LQD's distribution-adjusted daily return was flat, HYG gained 0.09% and EMB added 0.22%, even as long government bonds declined.

JPMorgan strategists led by Nathaniel Rosenbaum offered a constructive Q4 view in a note first published Friday and detailed Monday. They forecast the JULI investment-grade spread falling to 0.85 percentage point from Friday's 0.96, roughly corresponding to a 0.73-point Bloomberg U.S. corporate spread against Friday's 0.82. The argument relied on strong corporate earnings, less rate volatility and an improving balance between issuance and domestic and foreign demand as yields settled.

The bank expected about $305 billion of issuance over the remainder of the year, making Q4 the slowest quarter as is usual seasonally. A further $50 billion of hyperscaler debt could still arrive, but strategists regarded that amount as small relative to the technology companies' global issuance already completed this year. Their expected outperformance over Treasuries depended on fundamentals and slower supply; sensitivity to high financing costs still varied across borrowers.

Virgin Media O2 supplied an immediate exception to broad credit calm. Its U.S. junk bonds sank to record lows Monday, with a Virgin Media Finance 5% note losing 8 cents to trade as low as 42 cents. A Vmed O2 UK Financing euro note due in 2032 fell 6 cents to 70.5. The dollar notes were the leading decliners in the U.S. high-yield market.

The losses followed Friday's provisional Competition and Markets Authority objections to Nexfibre's proposed GBP2 billion combination with Netomnia. Virgin Media's owners Liberty Global and Telefonica are also two of Nexfibre's three shareholders. The planned combination would expand Virgin Media's network footprint and support its turnaround; Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Erhan Gurses said the plan counted on a GBP950 million net cash infusion. Blocking it could require more spending to upgrade Virgin Media's own fiber network, partly offset by avoided wholesale fees.

Monday's announcement that BT had acquired TalkTalk added a fresh competitive threat by expanding a major rival's customer base. Ironshield analyst Isharsimran Sawhney attributed Virgin Media's difficulties to competition, operating underperformance, weak free cash flow and substantial capital-expenditure requirements, all limiting debt reduction. The company reported approximately GBP22.5 billion, or $29 billion, of third-party debt and lease obligations at June's end. Its nearest maturity is in 2029, leaving the immediate repricing centered on the path to deleveraging rather than an imminent bond repayment.

Municipal issuers had more room to defer borrowing, but at a cost to planned refinancing savings. FHN Financial's public-finance head Ajay Thomas estimated that about $6 billion of refunding transactions were on hold or delayed as borrowers waited for lower yields. Benchmark 30-year municipal yields had reached about 5.26%, their highest since at least 2011, before easing to roughly 5.12% Monday. That retreat still left some refinancing plans uneconomic.

New Jersey's Transportation Trust Fund Authority had planned an approximately $1.7 billion refunding sale on October 1, but it did not price. The authority had $17.8 billion of debt outstanding at June's end and finances roads, bridges and mass transit, including New Jersey Transit. Philadelphia's school district moved a $450 million refunding planned for this week to a day-to-day schedule, according to PNC public-finance head Samantha Funk.

New York's Metropolitan Transportation Authority is seeking to refund $1 billion this month, subject to market conditions. Deputy chief of financial services Olga Chernat said in late-September remarks that the more significant concern was the cost of future new debt, which would be incorporated into the November financial plan. Refinancing can wait when its purpose is interest savings; new capital commitments face a different constraint if higher rates persist.

A smaller trade-finance development pointed to operational strain after lenders withdrew support. Employees of iron-ore trader Radiant World in Singapore, China and Europe said their September wages had not arrived on the usual late-month schedule as court-appointed managers assumed control of operations. Banks had cut off the trader after creditors raised concerns about financing obtained with allegedly falsified documents. The newly reported pay delays showed the disruption reaching day-to-day operations, beyond the earlier withdrawal of bank funding.

## Sovereign Outcomes Diverge From Brazil to Ukraine

Brazil's election produced one of the day's strongest fixed-income reactions. Flavio Bolsonaro won about 47% of Sunday's first-round vote against President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's roughly 45%, surprising investors who had generally expected Lula to lead. The candidates face a runoff October 25. Strong right-wing results in gubernatorial, congressional and Senate contests also changed the perceived prospects for implementing a fiscal program.

Swap contracts fell more than 100 basis points, the real rose almost 5% and the Ibovespa jumped 8% to a record. Brazil's dollar bonds were the best performers in emerging markets in Bloomberg's Monday account. Investors saw a higher likelihood of spending restraint and a credible fiscal anchor that could permit lower interest rates, rather than merely a change of president without legislative support.

UBS strategists Alejo Czerwonko and Luciano Telo made deeper and more durable fiscal adjustment their base case after the vote. UBS wealth-management economist Solange Srour said credible consolidation signals could produce a long-end rally narrowing spreads by as much as 250 basis points. That was a conditional estimate, while the realized swap move already reflected a substantial reassessment. Bolsonaro has yet to set out a detailed economic program, and the task of reducing spending remains distinct from investors' enthusiasm over the result.

Elsewhere, a stronger dollar and Europe's sovereign concerns produced less favorable outcomes. South Africa's 10-year yield rose to a six-month high and the rand weakened. Developing-market technology equities provided a counterweight, with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing rising more than 3% on possible collaboration with Elon Musk's Terafab. The differing responses left Brazilian fiscal optimism unusually powerful against a global backdrop of higher developed-market financing costs.

Turkey's new inflation release supported a different route toward lower rates. Annual consumer-price growth slowed for a fourth month to 29.7% from 31.5%, below Bloomberg's 30.3% survey median. Monthly inflation was 1.84%, unchanged from August and below the separate 2.28% expectation. Transportation, education and housing were among the largest monthly contributors. Two-year lira yields fell 36 basis points to 39.49%, and banking shares rose as much as 2.8%.

BBVA's Tufan Comert said improvement in both headline and core inflation strengthened the case for a cut at the October 22 meeting, while energy prices and geopolitical uncertainty argued for caution over its pace. MUFG Turkey's Onur Ilgen took the opposing view, expecting no October action without a significant decline in energy costs. Suppressed liquidity following the funds crisis was cooling activity and demand, but pressure on the lira could offset the disinflation if investors sought foreign currency. The current inflation surprise gave easing advocates new support without removing that disagreement.

Romanian assets rallied after S&P maintained BBB- on Friday rather than lowering the sovereign below investment grade. Domestic 10-year yields fell 12 basis points to 7.24% Monday, about 40 basis points below a week earlier. The Finance Ministry sold RON532 million, or $112 million, of 2028 bonds, exceeding its target and achieving its first successful target-sized sale since early September. The Bucharest equity benchmark gained 2.9%, while the leu strengthened 0.1% to around 5.334 per euro.

S&P retained a negative outlook and warned that prolonged political turmoil could obstruct deficit reduction over the next two years. Raiffeisen economist Stephan Imre said the scheduled annual reviews were now complete, shifting attention to consolidation in the 2027 budget, but unscheduled Q4 actions remained possible. President Nicusor Dan planned renewed talks with mainstream parties and could nominate another prime minister after two attempts to install a full government failed. The funding improvement followed the rating decision while government formation remained open.

India's sovereign curve faced the opposite policy direction. ICBC treasury head Alok Sharma expected the five- to 10-year gap to narrow toward 10 basis points as RBI liquidity withdrawal brought overnight rates nearer the repo rate. He said the curve could become flat or slightly inverted if overnight rates rose meaningfully above it. ICICI Securities Primary Dealership saw the five-year yield potentially rising toward 7% from 6.94% if tightening remained aggressive. These new curve forecasts specified where the already operating liquidity drain could exert pressure, rather than treating the withdrawal itself as a fresh announcement.

Japan's final September services survey showed a softer expansion with continuing labor demand. The index fell to 51.3 from 52.5, below the 51.6 flash reading, and the composite declined to 52.3 from 53.5, its lowest since May. New orders rose for a twenty-seventh month but more slowly, while new export business recorded its second-largest decline since January 2021. Employment increased for a thirteenth month, at its fastest rate since February, and backlogs grew at a seven-month high.

Japanese input-cost inflation eased to a six-month low but remained historically elevated, with raw materials, crude, labor and food contributing. Selling-price inflation also moderated. Canada's survey presented a weaker demand position: services activity rose to 48.3 from 46.8 but remained in contraction for a fourth month, and the composite increased to 48.7 from 47.8 without crossing 50. New business stood at 48.5, its fifth contracting month, and export weakness deepened.

Canadian input prices rose to 62.2 from 61.7, while future activity expectations improved to a five-month high of 61.4 from 56.4. S&P Global economist Paul Smith linked uncertainty, falling exports and higher operating costs to tariffs and the Iran war. Unlike the U.S. and euro-area surveys, Canada's release combined actual contraction with rising costs, making the growth-inflation trade-off less favorable even as confidence recovered.

Ukraine faced a more immediate financing squeeze. Reuters reported its most severe budget crisis since the full-scale invasion in 2022, with a $56 billion financing gap this year, approximately a quarter of GDP, including $27 billion for military spending. The government froze nonessential spending, including reconstruction of damaged buildings and infrastructure, to prioritize defense, public-sector wages and pensions.

Daily combat costs have risen to about $190 million from $140 million two years ago, excluding direct Western military aid. Defense expenditure exceeded $44 billion in the first nine months against tax receipts of about $42 billion. The government estimates that Russian attacks cost more than UAH49.5 billion, or approximately $1.1 billion, in tax revenue over that period, with the loss potentially reaching UAH70 billion by year-end.

Delayed tax and anti-corruption legislation has held up billions of euros in foreign loans. Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi said $29.5 billion of this year's aid was at risk. Ukraine is discussing earlier disbursement of an EU EUR90 billion loan scheduled for next year, but people familiar with the talks warned that bringing funds forward could transfer the pressure into 2027. The proposed defense budget for next year is a record $110 billion before direct military aid, and Finance Minister Sergii Marchenko puts the unfunded gap above $32 billion.

The borrowing problem is being reinforced by damage to the revenue base. Attacks have hit factories, warehouses, ports and railways, including steel production that represented about a tenth of prewar output. September grain exports fell 36.6% from a year earlier, and Economy Minister Oleksandr Kravchenko said around $40 billion of annual export revenue was at risk. Economists expect growth of only 0.5%-1.5% this year after 1.8% in 2025. Faster official financing could support immediate payments, but reform conditions and destruction of productive capacity remain separate constraints.

## Forward Market Significance

The U.S. Treasury auction cycle begins October 6 with a $58 billion three-year note sale at 1 p.m. New York time, followed by 10- and 30-year auctions later in the week. The longer maturities will test whether yields near multidecade highs attract sufficient demand after another session of duration losses. Their reception matters alongside a fresh technical warning that further long-end increases could change the bonds governing futures hedges.

BNP Paribas strategists Guneet Dhingra, Sebastian Mauleon and Vincent Zhou warned that a shift in the cheapest-to-deliver security toward a longer maturity could force additional futures adjustments. The current long-bond contract's cheapest deliverable is the 2.5% February 2045 Treasury; Bloomberg scenario analysis suggests a 30-year yield near 6% could shift it toward a 2050 maturity. Long futures holders seeking unchanged portfolio duration would need to sell, while short holders would need to buy back, leaving the net market effect dependent on the positions and timing.

The September 29 positioning snapshot showed asset managers cutting ultra-long net longs by almost 100,000 contracts in a week when 30-year yields rose from 5.28% to as high as 5.62%. Bloomberg valued the reduction at about $15 million per basis point of risk, equivalent to $11 billion of the current long bond. SMBC's Monty Gandhi said the ultra-long contract had already switched to a higher-duration deliverable, while the long-bond contract still faced extension risk. BMO Asset Management's Earl Davis separately forecast a 6% long-bond yield, potentially this month, arguing that volatility could reinforce selling. Neither the scenario nor his forecast establishes a mechanical intervention threshold.

October 6 also brings weekly ADP employment at 8:15 a.m. New York time, following a previous reading of 20,000. It will add a fresh recruitment observation after Monday's services hiring improvement. August trade data follows at 8:30 a.m.; consensus expects the deficit to widen to $102 billion from $88.6 billion. The import and export composition will bear on whether strong domestic demand is accompanied by a larger external drag rather than a uniform expansion across activity.

John Williams, Michelle Bowman and Lorie Logan are scheduled to speak October 6, at 9:05 a.m., 10:45 a.m. and 7 p.m. New York time respectively. Their new assessments will be important after services cost pressure rose and longer real yields increased, with interest-rate swaps in Monday's rates account assigning around a 25% chance to an October Fed increase and fully pricing a quarter-point move by December. September meeting minutes are due Wednesday and will illuminate the reasoning behind the increase already delivered, while the speeches can address the more recent information.

Wednesday's RBI decision is expected to raise the repo rate 25 basis points to 5.50%. The rate decision and guidance on liquidity absorption jointly matter to the curve forecasts: a higher policy rate without effective overnight transmission would differ from tighter funding conditions alongside further increases. In Europe, Germany's approaching November 1 gas-storage deadline gives Nagel's supply warning a specific horizon. Continued price acceleration alongside resilient services orders would constrain the ECB even if sovereign stress strengthened the case for a separate balance-sheet response.

Corporate demand faces defined deadlines. Everllence loan orders close October 13 and Volta commitments are due October 14, while Stonebriar's equipment ABS is expected to settle October 14. Their reception will show how readily investors absorb industrial leverage, unrated AI loans and diversified GPU collateral on different terms. For Virgin Media O2, the competition review and the consequences of BT's TalkTalk purchase remain more consequential than the generally firmer high-yield market; for municipal borrowers, a decline sufficient to restore refinancing savings could release transactions now waiting day to day.

Brazil's October 25 runoff leaves its sharp rally dependent on the electoral outcome and credible fiscal detail. Turkey's October 22 meeting confronts a lower inflation reading but continuing energy and currency risks. Ukraine's request for accelerated European financing has a different immediate test: whether disbursement timing and reform conditions can be reconciled before spending needs force further cuts elsewhere in the budget.

In the separate early Asian session Tuesday, Australian and New Zealand government bonds fell after the U.S. long-end selloff. Australia's 10-year yield rose 6 basis points to 5.39%, while Nasdaq 100 futures gained about 0.2%. The later trading carried the divergence between duration and technology-led equities into the Asian day, with Monday's completed U.S. session still defined by higher real long-term yields despite softer oil and firmer credit.

section_summaries.summary: Services demand and rising costs kept pressure on long Treasuries: 10- and 30-year yields rose 3.4 and 4.3 basis points as the 2-year fell 1.4, with real yields accounting for most of the 10-year increase and breakeven inflation slipping 0.1 basis points. Softer oil and modestly tighter U.S. corporate spreads did not reverse the move. French stress reached bank credit, Brazil rallied on fiscal hopes, and AI borrowing, delayed municipal refinancing and Virgin Media O2 losses showed increasingly divergent financing conditions.

section_summaries.summary: ISM services activity eased to 54.9, but hiring returned to expansion and prices paid reached 74.0; S&P Global services activity accelerated to 58.8. Both surveys showed backlogs and cost pressure rather than broad demand weakness. The 10-year real yield rose 3.5 basis points to 2.944%, with breakeven inflation slipping 0.1 basis points to 2.363%. Lower oil prices and technology-led equity gains offered little relief to duration.

section_summaries.market_read: Banks transmit sovereign stress through government-bond holdings and policies affecting borrowers, while fiscal repricing complicates central-bank intervention.
section_summaries.section_title: French Risk Spreads Into Banks as ECB Weighs Energy Pressure
section_summaries.summary: Societe Generale default protection became more expensive than Deutsche Bank's as French fiscal risk spread into bank funding and the euro touched a 17-month low. Spain called a November 29 election, while Japanese investors' large French bond exposure and hedging costs complicated renewed demand. ECB officials faced resilient services activity and renewed energy pressure, without clear broad wage-price pass-through; a proposal to pause bond runoff was not an ECB decision.

section_summaries.market_read: Amortization, lower loan-to-value ratios and diversified collateral distinguish equipment securitizations from financing backed entirely by GPUs.
section_summaries.section_title: AI Borrowing Reaches Loans and Equipment Securitizations
section_summaries.summary: Volta's $5 billion unrated AI loan was marketed at an approximately 11% yield, combining GPU purchases with lease support and limiting access to CLO buyers. Stonebriar's $869 million equipment ABS includes about 15% GPU collateral, extending AI exposure into diversified pools. Everllence acquisition loans and Schneider's $22.6 billion PTC agreement added demand for capital despite high financing costs, while the BOJ's Uchida left AI's eventual neutral-rate effect unresolved.

section_summaries.market_read: Municipal refinancing for interest savings can wait; persistent high yields still raise the cost of new capital commitments.
section_summaries.section_title: Refinancing Delays and Broadband Losses Divide Credit
section_summaries.summary: Modestly tighter U.S. corporate spreads and noticeably tighter hard-currency EM spreads contrasted with sharp Virgin Media O2 losses. Objections to Nexfibre's Netomnia deal threatened a planned GBP950 million cash infusion, while BT's TalkTalk acquisition added competition; the pressure centered on deleveraging, not an imminent maturity. Municipal borrowers delayed about $6 billion of refinancing because yields still prevented the savings sought, despite Monday's retreat.

section_summaries.next_check: Brazil's October 25 runoff and credible fiscal detail will determine whether the election-driven rally has support beyond the initial result.
section_summaries.section_title: Sovereign Outcomes Diverge From Brazil to Ukraine
section_summaries.summary: Brazilian swaps fell more than 100 basis points after Flavio Bolsonaro's surprise lead raised fiscal-consolidation hopes, though his program remained undefined. Turkish disinflation supported easing arguments, while Romania's retained investment-grade rating improved funding despite political uncertainty. India's liquidity withdrawal threatened curve flattening; Japan slowed and Canada remained in contraction. Ukraine's $56 billion financing gap combined delayed aid with damage to its revenue base.

Treasury auctions will test demand for longer maturities after the selloff, while a 30-year yield near 6% could change futures deliverables without a predetermined net selling effect. New U.S. labor data and Fed remarks will clarify the demand-policy tension. Germany's gas-storage deadline tests energy pressure alongside ECB fiscal concerns; October 13-14 financing deadlines will show investor appetite for industrial leverage, unrated AI loans and GPU-backed equipment pools.

overall_summary.headline: Long Treasury yields rise as resilient services demand sustains pressure on the real cost of capital
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Long-dated Treasuries lost ground on October 5 as September services surveys showed resilient demand, improving hiring and rising business costs. ISM activity eased to 54.9, but prices paid rose to 74.0, their highest since July 2022; S&P Global services activity reached 58.8, its strongest expansion since July 2021. Slower recruitment across the broader economy had not translated into sufficient demand relief to ease price-setting pressure.

The 10- and 30-year Treasury yields rose 3.4 and 4.3 basis points, to 5.307% and 5.664%, while the 2-year fell 1.4 basis points to 4.813%. The 2s10s curve widened 4.8 basis points to 49.4. At 10 years, the real yield rose 3.5 basis points to 2.944%, with breakeven inflation slipping 0.1 basis points to 2.363%: higher real borrowing costs accounted for most of the nominal yield rise. Oil fell roughly 2% and equities advanced. U.S. investment-grade and high-yield spreads tightened modestly, while hard-currency emerging-market spreads tightened noticeably, without preventing the long Treasury selloff.

French fiscal stress became more visible in bank credit, with Societe Generale default protection costing more than comparable Deutsche Bank protection, while the euro touched a 17-month low. Resilient euro-area services activity and renewed energy pressure complicated the ECB's response. Brazil moved in the opposite direction: Flavio Bolsonaro's unexpected first-round lead sent swap rates down more than 100 basis points on hopes for fiscal consolidation, although his detailed economic program remained unset.

Borrowing continued on increasingly differentiated terms. Volta's $5 billion AI loan was marketed at an approximately 11% yield, and GPU exposure entered diversified equipment securitizations. Municipal borrowers delayed about $6 billion of refinancing, while Virgin Media O2 bonds plunged as a regulatory obstacle and stronger competition threatened deleveraging. This week's longer Treasury auctions will test demand after another rise in long-term financing costs.
overall_summary.summary: Stronger services hiring, backlogs and cost pressure left long-term real borrowing rates higher with broadly flat inflation compensation, despite softer oil and firmer credit, while French fiscal stress spread into bank funding and expensive financing increasingly separated borrowers.
